id: title:jabahamondes:enable setup for the new dashboard rollout

review.posthog_relevance: Supports a phased rollout and compatibility between legacy and new marketing analytics dashboard variants, allowing the Setup section to appear when either the legacy or new dashboard feature flag is active.
review.reason: The change implements a bounded, substantive improvement: it updates the backend availability check, frontend TypeScript checks, and documentation to support two alternative feature flags instead of one. This preserves compatibility while enabling a phased rollout, which is a reliability and operational improvement. No tier 3 systemic risk reduction or tier 1 narrow-only change is;
review.uncertainty: The actual benefit depends on the successful implementation and adoption of the new dashboard, which is not independently verified by this code change. The score reflects the implementation and compatibility support, not the outcome of the new dashboard's performance or user benefit.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No missing context or unrelated PRs detected. No tier assignment performed; score and confidence withheld.

observations.behavior: Documentation updated to reflect that Setup availability now depends on either the legacy flag or the new dashboard flag.
observations.code_quote: Setup is available when either `marketing-analytics-setup` or `new-marketing-analytics-dashboard` is enabled for the requesting person. Both Setup endpoints use the same rule; existing project permissions still apply.
observations.posthog_connection: Documentation warning for users and support; does not change runtime behavior.

observations.behavior: Frontend TypeScript now checks both feature flags to determine if the Setup section is enabled, rather than only the legacy flag.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows the UI to appear when either the legacy or the new dashboard flag is active, supporting a phased rollout or coexistence of two dashboard variants.

observations.behavior: Backend helper `_setup_enabled` now evaluates both flags and returns true if either is enabled, while preserving the original single-flag behavior for the first flag.
observations.posthog_connection: Changes the server-side availability check to support both flags, while retaining compatibility with the existing single-flag evaluation path.
